companies.name: Bury Council
companies.legacy_system: Aareon QL housing management (on-premise modules, no self-service)
companies.evidence_quote: This significant management change has, since 2023, highlighted clear and present housing IT issues.
companies.forced_admin_job: Housing officers re-key tenancy, repairs and arrears data across QL screens and spreadsheets; the council is funding a dedicated Aareon employee plus a year-one subscription simply to keep the screens working.
companies.why_archaic_helps: Cabinet has just approved £660k of revenue and £1.2m of HRA capital to patch QL rather than replace it, so there is budget in-year and no appetite for a two-year system programme; a screen-driving desk can start on the existing QL build in weeks.

companies.name: West Northamptonshire Council
companies.sector: Local authority - housing management (with ALMO Northamptonshire Partnership Homes)
companies.evidence_quote: Capita Open Housing is the primary IT solution used for managing housing stock in West Northamptonshire by the Council and its arm's length management organisation (ALMO) Northamptonshire Partnership Homes.
companies.forced_admin_job: Repairs ordering, voids, allocations and rent statements are all driven through Open Housing screens by hand, with the same household data entered by council and ALMO staff in separate workflows.
companies.why_archaic_helps: The Capita contract expires on 31 March 2026 and procurement of a replacement is only at market-exploration stage, so there is a two-to-three year gap where the only way to remove manual load is to automate the current screens.

companies.name: Royal Borough of Windsor and Maidenhead
companies.evidence_quote: This report recommends the continued use of an updated Unit 4 Agresso Finance system and its transition to a Cloud based version.
companies.forced_admin_job: Purchase orders, goods receipting, journal postings and budget-monitor reconciliations are keyed into Agresso by finance staff and budget holders, with monthly monitoring packs assembled by hand from Agresso extracts.
companies.why_archaic_helps: The council has explicitly chosen to stay on Agresso and upgrade rather than replace, which locks in the screen estate for years; automation of the posting and reconciliation work sits on top of the existing build with no migration.

companies.name: Hinckley & Bosworth Borough Council
companies.sector: Local authority - housing assets and repairs
companies.legacy_system: Orchard housing management plus Integrator asset management (no interface)
companies.evidence_quote: This means that all data has to be input manually into both systems as repairs and/or improvements are completed.
companies.forced_admin_job: Every completed repair or improvement is keyed twice - once into Orchard and again into Integrator - by different officers depending on job role, with reconciliation done by hand.
companies.why_archaic_helps: The council's own paper puts the cost of fixing the double-keying at a capital purchase plus £5,000 a year, which it declined; a screen-driving desk removes the duplicate entry at a fraction of a system replacement and needs no interface project.

companies.name: believe housing
companies.evidence_quote: You will assist with the effective operation and development of the financial management system OpenAccounts and the ongoing development of the Ebis module (Online workflow management system).
companies.forced_admin_job: Finance assistants key invoices, accruals and journals into OpenAccounts and then push the same items through Ebis workflow for authorisation, re-entering data to produce statutory accounts working papers.
companies.why_archaic_helps: OpenAccounts is a green-screen-era ledger with no meaningful API; a desk that reads and writes the same screens can take the invoice-to-journal and accruals work without touching the ledger or waiting for a finance transformation programme.

companies.name: Birmingham City University
companies.size: More than 3,000 academic and professional staff
companies.evidence_quote: the postholder will contribute to the configuration and development of the University's student record system (SITS:Vision).
companies.forced_admin_job: Registry staff manually key module changes, assessment marks, award outcomes and curriculum amendments into SITS screens, then re-check them against spreadsheets before board reports.

decision_maker.name: Andy Winter
decision_maker.role: Director of Student and Academic Services

companies.why_archaic_helps: SITS is retained and being extended, not replaced, so the manual data entry into its screens persists; an agent that works the SITS client removes the keying load without an integration project or a student-record migration.

companies.name: University of York
companies.evidence_quote: The team is responsible for the configuration, development, management and maintenance of our student record system (SITS) and its integrations with other business systems.
companies.forced_admin_job: Professional services staff key module registrations, marks and progression decisions into SITS and then re-enter the same data into departmental spreadsheets and returns.

decision_maker.name: Tom Banham
decision_maker.role: Academic Registrar and Director of Student Education and Experience

companies.why_archaic_helps: York is investing in SITS staff rather than replacing the platform, which means screen-bound processes for at least another contract cycle; a desk that drives SITS absorbs termly peaks (enrolment, assessment boards) without headcount.

companies.name: University of Bath
companies.evidence_quote: Senior Developer (SITS) - Department Digital, Data & Technology Group - Starting from £39,560, rising to £46,970
companies.forced_admin_job: Registry and faculty staff key unit registrations, assessment marks and progression outcomes into SITS by hand, with exception reports worked from Excel downloads.
companies.why_archaic_helps: Bath is recruiting permanent SITS developers, signalling a multi-year commitment to the platform; the cheaper win is automating the keying work around SITS rather than replacing it, and the CDO owns both budgets.

companies.name: University of Cumbria
companies.evidence_quote: SITS is the University's student record system and is central to the effective administration of the student lifecycle.
companies.forced_admin_job: A small Student Systems and Data team hand-keys and checks student records across four campuses, including placement and progression data, with reconciliation against spreadsheets.

decision_maker.name: Bronia Sledz
decision_maker.role: Head of Student Systems and Data

companies.why_archaic_helps: A distributed multi-campus university with a thin central team cannot afford a student-record replacement; a screen-driving desk scales the manual keying and checking that SITS forces, at a fraction of a programme.

companies.name: University of Plymouth
companies.evidence_quote: SITS Developer - Plymouth - 08/04/2026
companies.forced_admin_job: Faculty and registry administrators key enrolments, module selections, marks and mitigating-circumstances outcomes into SITS screens, then duplicate the data into local trackers.
companies.why_archaic_helps: Plymouth keeps hiring SITS developers rather than moving platform, so the screen work is stable for years; automation of the keying and checking removes seasonal backlog without a vendor migration.

companies.name: Guildhall School of Music & Drama
companies.evidence_quote: The role holder will play a key role in managing the student lifecycle in SITS from the point of enrolment through to graduation, taking the lead on enrolment events.
companies.forced_admin_job: Registry staff key enrolment, one-to-one lesson allocations, assessment marks and progression decisions into SITS by hand, then reconcile against departmental spreadsheets before boards.

decision_maker.name: Jo Hutchinson
decision_maker.role: Director of Student & Academic Services and Registrar

companies.why_archaic_helps: A small conservatoire registry with a bespoke, performance-heavy timetable cannot buy a new student system; a screen-driving desk absorbs the manual SITS entry and reconciliation instead.

companies.name: West Herts College
companies.evidence_quote: Maintain good working knowledge of college learner record system (ProSolution).
companies.forced_admin_job: MIS officers key enrolment, attendance and achievement data into ProSolution, then re-work it in Excel for funding returns, audits and data-integrity checks.
companies.why_archaic_helps: College funding depends on error-free ILR data keyed into ProSolution; an agent that works the ProSolution screens for attendance and achievement reconciliation protects funding without an MIS replacement.

companies.name: Craven College
companies.evidence_quote: Develop and maintain the college's MIS platform (currently ProSolution) and other management information systems and records.
companies.forced_admin_job: MIS staff key learner and attendance data into ProSolution and then rebuild reports in Excel and other systems for funding, timetabling and quality reviews.
companies.why_archaic_helps: A 259-FTE college cannot fund an MIS replacement, and the word 'currently' in its own job spec concedes the platform is provisional; screen automation delivers the data-quality gain now on the existing system.

companies.name: Richmond upon Thames College
companies.evidence_quote: Review reports and attendance data from ProSolution to analyse room occupancy and utilisation.
companies.forced_admin_job: The timetabling officer exports ProSolution attendance and register data, then manually rebuilds occupancy and utilisation analysis for room planning and funding audits.
companies.why_archaic_helps: A single-campus college with a fixed MIS budget will not replace ProSolution; an agent that pulls registers, chases missing attendance and rebuilds the utilisation reports removes the manual grind.

companies.forced_admin_job: Billing and e-billing staff key time entries, disbursements and write-offs into Elite 3E, reconcile them against client e-billing portals, and rebuild reports in Power BI.
companies.why_archaic_helps: Elite 3E's billing workflows are screen-bound and portal reconciliation is manual copy-and-key; an agent removes the reconciliation load without a finance-system replacement, and the CFO owns the revenue-leakage case.

companies.why_archaic_helps: Fletchers is hiring Proclaim developer capacity to automate workflows it cannot buy off the shelf; a screen desk delivers that automation on the live Proclaim build without waiting for internal development.

method_notes: Evidence was gathered between 19 and 21 October 2026 from primary sources only: council cabinet and committee reports (Bury, West Northamptonshire, Windsor & Maidenhead, Hinckley & Bosworth), university and college job descriptions PDFs (BCU, Cumbria, Ravensbourne, Craven, West Herts, RUTC), live vacancy pages (York, Bath, Plymouth, Guildhall, Forbes, Flint Bishop, Brodies, Carpenters, Bond Turner, Kennedys, Fletchers, Saffery, Express), one Find a Tender notice (Sheffield Hallam) and one council workforce/accounts document per authority for headcount. Every legacy-system claim is tied to a quotation naming the product; no system was inferred from sector or vendor list. Quotations are verbatim from the cited page as retrieved; where a vacancy carries no publication date the evidence_date records the access date. Headcounts are the employer's own FTE or headcount figure where published (Bury, RBWM, Hinckley, Craven), the employer's own claim where stated (York, Bath's DDaT page equivalents, Plymouth, Guildford, BCU, Sheffield Hallam via The Conversation profile), or a third-party estimate (Revelio Labs, Growjo, LeadIQ, LinkedIn) clearly labelled as such. Four entries rest on evidence older than 2024 (Hinckley 2015, RUTC 2019, Craven 2023, believe housing 2023); they were kept because the citation explicitly names the product and the forced manual task, but the current system estate should be confirmed on first contact. Sizes outside the 50-3,000 target band (York, Bath, Sheffield Hallam, Kennedys) were retained only where the legacy evidence is unusually strong and the buyer sits at group or director level. All organisations are UK-registered or UK public bodies; Saffery's cited vacancy is in its Dublin office but the firm is UK-headquartered and runs one Elite 3E instance.
